sections.challenge: The manual process of entering Bill of Materials (BOM) data from PDFs and images into the SQL database was extremely time-consuming and prone to human error. A single document took an average of 8 minutes (5-6 minutes for data entry and 1-2 minutes for verification), limiting productivity to only 6-7 documents per hour.
sections.solution:
We designed and implemented an AI-powered OCR system to automate the data extraction process. The solution leverages a multi-stage pipeline that includes:

The system consists of three main components:


1. **Table Detection**

   


- Uses object detection model
   


- Identifies and isolates table structures
   


- Detects key data fields and layouts


  - Processes multiple table formats


2. **Data Extraction**


   - Utilizes **PaddleOCR** for text recognition


   - Employs **PaddleStructure** for structural analysis


  - Uses **Docling PDF Extractor** for PDF parsing


   - Handles both textual and structured data


3. **Data Validation**


  - Powered by **Qwen2.5-VL-32B** model


   - Validates extracted data accuracy


   - Reconstructs complete tables


   - Ensures data consistency
sections.impact: This automated pipeline significantly reduced the time required for data processing and increased overall productivity. The time per document was cut down to just 1-2 minutes, boosting the workload from 6-7 PDFs per hour to 15 PDFs per hour. In the future, we aim to further improve the pipeline's accuracy to enable direct data integration into the database.

metrics.description: Minimized human error in data entry

sections.challenge: The organization relied on a commercial SIEM solution (Splunk) that was expensive to maintain, with annual licensing costs reaching nearly 800,000 THB. Security analysts faced difficulties in conducting real-time investigations due to limited customization, and compliance reporting was largely manual, leading to delays and increased workload. The lack of a cost-effective and flexible solution created operational inefficiencies and budgetary strain.
sections.solution: The team implemented an in-house Wazuh SIEM solution, replacing the costly Splunk platform. Wazuh provided centralized log management, threat detection, and compliance reporting at a fraction of the cost. The open-source nature of Wazuh allowed full customization to fit organizational needs, while integration with existing infrastructure enabled continuous monitoring and automated alerts. To ensure operational reliability, the system was set up with 24/7 monitoring responsibilities assigned to the internal security team and supported by i-Net.
sections.impact: The implementation of Wazuh SIEM significantly reduced operational costs while strengthening the organization's cybersecurity posture. By eliminating the annual 800,000 THB Splunk license, the project delivered direct cost savings and allowed budget reallocation to other IT priorities. Automated log collection and real-time monitoring improved incident response efficiency, reducing investigation time from hours to minutes. Compliance audits became faster and more accurate through built-in reporting features, ensuring the organization met regulatory requirements without the burden of manual work.

metrics.description: Annual savings from replacing Splunk with Wazuh

sections.challenge: The IT & Data Management department faced significant challenges in knowledge management and documentation accessibility. Team members had to navigate through multiple scattered documentation sources including various wikis, shared drives, and individual team repositories to find project information, technical guides, and standard operating procedures. This fragmented approach led to duplicated efforts, inconsistent documentation standards, and difficulty in onboarding new team members. Additionally, there was no centralized location to showcase completed projects and their technical implementations, making it challenging to leverage past experiences and best practices across different teams and initiatives.
sections.solution: Developed IT-PORTAL using Docusaurus, a modern React-based static site generator optimized for documentation websites. The solution provides a comprehensive knowledge management platform with multiple organized sections including IT Management (project workflows and Asana guides), IT Development (coding standards and technical documentation), Data Management (AWS guides, Customer Data Platform documentation), and tutorial sections for team onboarding. The platform features full-text search capabilities, responsive mobile design, Markdown/MDX support for rich content creation, automated deployment pipelines, and integrated content submission forms. Built with modern web technologies including React, TailwindCSS for styling, and Playwright for end-to-end testing, ensuring reliability and maintainability.
sections.impact: IT-PORTAL has revolutionized knowledge management within the IT & Data Management department by establishing a centralized, searchable documentation hub that significantly improves team efficiency and collaboration. The platform has standardized documentation practices across all teams, reduced onboarding time for new team members from weeks to days, and eliminated the time-consuming process of searching through multiple repositories for technical information. With comprehensive AWS guides, project management workflows, and coding standards all accessible in one location, the platform has enhanced decision-making capabilities and accelerated project delivery. The mobile-responsive design ensures that critical documentation and project information are available to team members whether they're in the office or working remotely, supporting modern hybrid work environments.
